data.narrative:
Vention is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Etienne Lacroix and Max Windisch, having raised $95M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—operating in the same sector and stage band, including Hadrian, Nimble Robotics, Exotec, and Dexterity.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised ($95M) as a baseline proxy and applying a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $162M. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Exotec at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, Hadrian at $1.6B, and Nimble Robotics at $1.0B) yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The divergence between these methods reflects meaningful heterogeneity in how the peer cohort has been valued.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $137M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median point of $906M. Key uncertainties include relative capital efficiency versus peers, market positioning within the robotics subsector, and whether the target company's commercial traction and customer concentration align with the higher-valued peers or the lower-valued comparables.
